question: Which classic 1950s sitcom featured bandleader Ricky Ricardo and his scheming redheaded wife?
hint: Desi Arnaz played Ricky, opposite his real-life wife.
funFact: The 1953 episode where Lucy has her baby drew about 44 million viewers, more than watched President Eisenhower's inauguration the next day.

question: Which band made its live US TV debut on The Ed Sullivan Show in February 1964?
hint: They opened with “All My Loving.”
funFact: About 73 million Americans tuned in, roughly 60 percent of all the TV sets switched on that night.

question: In the original Star Trek, what is the name of Captain Kirk's starship?
hint: Its registry number is NCC-1701.
funFact: The original series ran for just three seasons (1966–69) but launched one of TV's biggest franchises.

question: Which Sesame Street Muppet lives in a trash can?
hint: His pet worm is named Slimey.
funFact: Puppeteer Caroll Spinney played both him and Big Bird from the show's 1969 debut until 2018.

question: Which boxer, born Cassius Clay, promised to “float like a butterfly, sting like a bee”?
hint: He liked to call himself “The Greatest.”
funFact: He lit the Olympic cauldron at the 1996 Atlanta Games.

question: What 1975 Steven Spielberg thriller made beachgoers afraid to go back in the water?
hint: John Williams wrote its famous two-note theme.
funFact: The crew nicknamed the troublesome mechanical shark “Bruce,” after Spielberg's lawyer.

question: On which TV game show does the announcer shout “Come on down!”?
hint: Plinko is one of its most famous games.
funFact: Bob Barker hosted it for 35 years, from 1972 to 2007.

question: Which brothers' group sang “Stayin' Alive” on the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack?
hint: They were famous for soaring falsetto harmonies.
funFact: Its tempo falls within the 100–120 beats per minute recommended for CPR chest compressions, so it's used to help teach CPR.

question: In Top Gun (1986), what is Tom Cruise's pilot call sign?
hint: His radar officer and best friend is called Goose.
funFact: The sequel arrived 36 years later, in 2022.

question: In Super Mario Bros., what is the name of Mario's brother?
hint: He's taller than Mario and dresses in green.
funFact: Mario's first appearance was in Donkey Kong (1981), where he was called Jumpman.

question: What twisting puzzle cube, invented in Hungary, became a worldwide craze around 1980?
hint: Each of its six faces has nine colored squares.
funFact: It can be scrambled more than 43 quintillion ways, yet every position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.

question: Which Friends character's catchphrase is “How you doin'?”
hint: He plays Dr. Drake Ramoray on Days of Our Lives.
funFact: Matt LeBlanc kept playing him in the spin-off series Joey (2004–06).

question: In The Lion King (1994), what is the name of Simba's villainous uncle?
hint: He sings “Be Prepared.”
funFact: Simba's father, Mufasa, was voiced by James Earl Jones, also the voice of Darth Vader.

question: Which basketball legend was nicknamed “His Airness”?
hint: He won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls.
funFact: Nike released his first signature sneaker, the Air Jordan, in 1985.

question: What is the name of SpongeBob SquarePants's pet snail?
hint: He meows like a cat.
funFact: Creator Stephen Hillenburg taught marine biology before he became an animator.

question: In Shrek (2001), what does Shrek say ogres have in common with onions?
hint: Donkey suggests cakes and parfaits instead.
funFact: Shrek won the first-ever Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

question: Which actor played Tony Stark in the Iron Man films?
hint: He also played Sherlock Holmes in two Guy Ritchie films.
funFact: Iron Man (2008) was the first film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

question: In the US version of The Office, which Pennsylvania city is the Dunder Mifflin branch in?
hint: Its nickname is “the Electric City.”
funFact: The show was adapted from the British original, created by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant in 2001.

question: Which talk-show host shouted “You get a car!” as she gave every audience member a new car in 2004?
hint: Her show ran for 25 seasons, ending in 2011.
funFact: All 276 people in the studio audience received a new Pontiac G6.

question: In Despicable Me (2010), what are Gru's little yellow, goggle-wearing helpers called?
hint: Three of the best known are Kevin, Stuart and Bob.
funFact: Co-director Pierre Coffin voices most of them, in gibberish sprinkled with real words from languages such as Spanish, French and Italian.

question: In which blocky building game do players dodge hissing, exploding green Creepers?
hint: Its classic default characters are Steve and Alex.
funFact: Microsoft bought the game's maker, Mojang, for $2.5 billion in 2014.

question: On July 21, 2023, fans made a double feature of Barbie and which other blockbuster released the same day?
hint: Christopher Nolan directed it.
funFact: Fans nicknamed the double bill “Barbenheimer,” and Oppenheimer went on to win Best Picture.

question: Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics?
hint: It last hosted the Summer Games exactly 100 years earlier, in 1924.
funFact: It was the first Summer Olympics opening ceremony held outside a stadium: athletes paraded on boats along the Seine.

question: Which Addams Family daughter got her own Netflix series in 2022, starring Jenna Ortega?
hint: Her brother is Pugsley.
funFact: Jenna Ortega choreographed the show's viral dance scene herself, set to The Cramps' “Goo Goo Muck.”

question: Which breakfast cereal's cartoon mascots are three elves named Snap, Crackle and Pop?
hint: Their names copy the sounds it makes when you pour on the milk.
funFact: In the 1950s the trio briefly had a fourth elf in their ads, named Pow.

question: Which Danish company makes colorful interlocking plastic toy bricks?
hint: Stepping on one barefoot is famously painful.
funFact: The name comes from the Danish words “leg godt,” meaning “play well.”

question: Which candy's famous slogan promises it “melts in your mouth, not in your hand”?
hint: Its cartoon mascots include Red and Yellow.
funFact: The two M's stand for the founders, Forrest Mars and Bruce Murrie.

question: Which actor first played James Bond on the big screen, in Dr. No (1962)?
hint: This Scotsman once delivered milk in Edinburgh.
funFact: Ian Fleming borrowed the name James Bond from an American bird expert whose book he owned.

question: What 34-letter word did Mary Poppins sing about in 1964?
hint: “Even though the sound of it is something quite atrocious…”
funFact: Mary Poppins was Julie Andrews's first film, and it won her the Oscar for Best Actress.

question: To which US president did Marilyn Monroe famously sing “Happy Birthday” in 1962?
hint: The gala came 10 days before his 45th birthday.
funFact: Her sparkling gown sold at auction in 2016 for about $4.8 million.

question: The 1983 finale of which TV comedy, set in an Army hospital during the Korean War, drew about 106 million US viewers?
hint: Alan Alda played Hawkeye Pierce.
funFact: The series ran 11 seasons, more than three times as long as the Korean War itself.

question: Which Swedish group won Eurovision in 1974 with “Waterloo”?
hint: The band's name is made from its members' first initials.
funFact: In 2022 they launched ABBA Voyage, a London concert show starring digital avatars of the band.

question: In Star Wars (1977), what is the name of Han Solo's ship?
hint: It “made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs.”
funFact: Harrison Ford had been working as a carpenter between acting jobs before Star Wars made him a star.

question: What 1972 Atari arcade game had players bat a blip back and forth with on-screen paddles?
hint: It's basically electronic table tennis.
funFact: The first test machine, in a California bar, broke down because its coin box was overflowing with quarters.

question: Which soft drink's 1971 TV ad featured a hilltop choir singing “I'd like to teach the world to sing”?
hint: The final episode of Mad Men ends with this ad.
funFact: The jingle was rerecorded as a full song, “I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing (In Perfect Harmony),” and became a hit single.

question: In Back to the Future, what speed must the DeLorean reach to travel through time?
hint: It also needs 1.21 gigawatts of electricity.
funFact: Eric Stoltz was first cast as Marty McFly and filmed for weeks before Michael J. Fox replaced him.

question: In 1980's “Miracle on Ice,” the US Olympic hockey team stunned which heavily favored nation?
hint: Commentator Al Michaels: “Do you believe in miracles? Yes!”
funFact: It wasn't the gold-medal game: the US clinched gold two days later by beating Finland.

question: What egg-shaped digital pet from Japan had to be fed and cleaned up after, or it would die?
hint: Bandai released it in 1996.
funFact: Its name blends the Japanese word for egg, “tamago,” with the English word “watch.”

question: Disney released Toy Story (1995), the first fully computer-animated feature, but which studio actually made it?
hint: Its logo features a hopping desk lamp.
funFact: Steve Jobs bought it from Lucasfilm in 1986, and Disney bought it outright for $7.4 billion in 2006.

question: What was Sony's first home video game console?
hint: It launched in Japan in December 1994.
funFact: It grew out of a failed deal to build a CD-ROM add-on for Nintendo's Super NES.

question: Which Nintendo console, launched in 2006, had families swinging motion-sensing remotes to play bowling and tennis?
hint: Its code name during development was “Revolution.”
funFact: In most countries, Wii Sports came packed in the box with the console.

question: What Australian cartoon follows a young puppy, her little sister Bingo and their dad, Bandit?
hint: Their mum is called Chilli.
funFact: The title character is a Blue Heeler, and the show is made in Brisbane by Ludo Studio.

question: What is the name of the hidden African nation in Black Panther (2018)?
hint: It's rich in the fictional metal vibranium.
funFact: Black Panther was the first superhero film nominated for the Best Picture Oscar.

question: In 2015, the internet argued over a photo of a dress many saw as white and gold. What colors was it really?
hint: Its maker, the UK store Roman Originals, settled the argument.
funFact: Roman Originals later made a one-off white-and-gold version and auctioned it for the charity Comic Relief.

question: In 2012, which K-pop song became the first YouTube video to reach one billion views?
hint: Its singer did a horse-riding dance.
funFact: The title pokes fun at the flashy, newly rich lifestyle of Seoul's Gangnam district.

question: Which British singer named her albums 19, 21, 25 and 30?
hint: Her hits include “Rolling in the Deep” and “Hello.”
funFact: Her James Bond theme “Skyfall” won the Oscar for Best Original Song.

question: Which Kansas City Chiefs tight end began dating Taylor Swift in 2023?
hint: He hosts the New Heights podcast with his brother Jason.
funFact: Before they met, he went to her Kansas City concert hoping to give her a friendship bracelet with his phone number on it.

question: What 2021 Korean Netflix drama has cash-strapped contestants play a deadly version of Red Light, Green Light?
hint: Players wear green tracksuits; the guards wear pink.
funFact: Star Lee Jung-jae became the first Asian actor to win the Emmy for Lead Actor in a Drama Series.

question: What daily five-letter guessing game did The New York Times buy in 2022?
hint: Green tiles mean the right letter in the right spot.
funFact: Software engineer Josh Wardle made it for his partner, and its name is a pun on his surname.

question: Which 2025 Netflix animated movie gave us the chart-topping song “Golden”?
hint: Its singing heroines are Rumi, Mira and Zoey.
funFact: “Golden,” sung by the film's fictional group HUNTR/X, reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 2025.

question: Which brand's 40-ounce “Quencher” tumbler became a must-have craze in 2023?
hint: The company traces its vacuum bottles back to 1913.
funFact: After a viral video showed one surviving a car fire with ice still rattling inside, the company bought the owner a new car.

question: On the classic US Monopoly board, which property is the most expensive to buy?
hint: It's dark blue and sits just before “Go.”
funFact: The US board's street names come from Atlantic City, New Jersey.

question: On Gilligan's Island, what was the name of the tour boat that got shipwrecked?
hint: It shares its name with a tiny fish.
funFact: Creator Sherwood Schwartz reportedly named it after Newton Minow, the FCC chairman who had called TV “a vast wasteland,” as a jab.

question: The Etch A Sketch, a hit toy launched in 1960, was invented by an electrician from which country?
hint: Its inventor called it “the Magic Screen” in his own language.
funFact: André Cassagnes named it L'Écran Magique; the Ohio Art Company renamed it Etch A Sketch.

question: Which singer shocked folk fans by “going electric” at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival?
hint: He later won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
funFact: Timothée Chalamet played him in the 2024 film A Complete Unknown.

question: What 1975 fad gift came in a cardboard carrier with breathing holes and a training manual, but never needed feeding?
hint: Commands like “sit” and “stay” were very easy to teach it.
funFact: Its creator, California ad man Gary Dahl, became a millionaire almost overnight.

question: Which tennis champion beat Bobby Riggs in the 1973 “Battle of the Sexes” match?
hint: She won 39 Grand Slam titles across singles, doubles and mixed doubles.
funFact: Emma Stone played her in the 2017 film Battle of the Sexes.

question: In E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982), what candy does Elliott use to lure E.T.?
hint: The little candy-coated pieces come in orange, yellow and brown.
funFact: Drew Barrymore, who played Elliott's little sister Gertie, was six during filming.

question: Tetris got its name from the Greek “tetra,” meaning four, plus which sport, creator Alexey Pajitnov's favorite?
hint: It's a racket sport that, like Tetris, starts with “Te.”
funFact: Pajitnov made the game in Moscow in 1984; in 1989 it came packed in the box with Nintendo's first Game Boy in the US.

question: What was the first music video MTV played when it launched in 1981?
answer: “Video Killed the Radio Star” by The Buggles
hint: It was a 1979 UK No. 1 for the British duo The Buggles.
funFact: MTV's very first words on air were “Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll.”

question: Apple's famous “1984” Super Bowl ad was directed by which film director?
hint: He also directed Alien and Gladiator.
funFact: The ad launched the Macintosh computer and aired nationally only once, during Super Bowl XVIII.

question: In Ghostbusters (1984), what giant, sailor-suited monster stomps through New York at the climax?
hint: Ray summons it by picturing the most harmless thing from his childhood.
funFact: The gooey “melted marshmallow” that splattered the city and the cast was really shaving cream.

question: Which internet company's “You've got mail!” greeting inspired the title of a 1998 Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan film?
hint: It mailed out millions of free trial discs.
funFact: The famous voice belonged to Elwood Edwards, whose wife worked at the company.

question: What was Amazon's original name when Jeff Bezos founded it in 1994?
hint: It was a shortened version of a magician's magic word.
funFact: His lawyer misheard it as “cadaver,” so Bezos renamed it after the South American river.

question: Which 1990s boy band's name doubles as a play on the last letters of its original members' first names?
hint: Justin Timberlake was a member.
funFact: The name came from Justin Timberlake's mother, who remarked how “in sync” their voices sounded.

question: Who won the very first season of American Idol in 2002?
hint: Her later hits include “Since U Been Gone.”
funFact: The original judges were Simon Cowell, Paula Abdul and Randy Jackson.

question: Being “Rickrolled” means being tricked into watching the video for which 1987 song?
answer: “Never Gonna Give You Up” by Rick Astley
hint: It hit No. 1 in both the UK and the US.
funFact: In 2008 Astley pulled off a real-life Rickroll, popping out of a float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade mid-broadcast to lip-sync the song.

question: The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, “Me at the zoo” (2005), shows a co-founder standing in front of which animals?
hint: It was filmed at the San Diego Zoo.
funFact: Co-founder Jawed Karim posted the 19-second clip on April 23, 2005.

question: Which Las Vegas band sings the 2000s sing-along anthem “Mr. Brightside”?
hint: Their frontman is Brandon Flowers.
funFact: The song first came out in 2003 and appeared on their 2004 debut album, Hot Fuss.

question: What is golfer Tiger Woods's real first name?
hint: His father gave him his famous nickname in honor of a fellow soldier.
funFact: In 1997, aged 21, he became the youngest player ever to win the Masters.

question: Which emoji did Oxford Dictionaries choose as its 2015 Word of the Year?
hint: Oxford said it made up about one in five emojis sent in the UK that year.
funFact: It was the first time a pictograph, rather than a word, was named Word of the Year.

question: In Downton Abbey, what is the surname of the Earl of Grantham's family?
hint: His daughters are Lady Mary, Lady Edith and Lady Sybil.
funFact: The grand house is really Highclere Castle in Hampshire, England.

question: In the Broadway musical Hamilton, which character narrates much of the story and ends up facing Hamilton in a fatal duel?
hint: He was Thomas Jefferson's first vice president.
funFact: Hamilton won 11 Tony Awards in 2016, and Leslie Odom Jr. won Best Actor in a Musical for playing this role.

question: In 2023, who became the first Asian woman to win the Best Actress Oscar, for Everything Everywhere All at Once?
hint: She also starred in Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon and Crazy Rich Asians.
funFact: She was crowned Miss Malaysia in 1983, before her film career took off in Hong Kong.

question: Beyoncé won her first Album of the Year Grammy in 2025 for which country-flavored album?
hint: It includes her cover of Dolly Parton's “Jolene.”
funFact: It also made her the first Black artist to win the Grammy for Best Country Album.
